verdicts.quote: The import is **all-or-nothing**: if any row is invalid, no user is created and every problem is reported at once.
every response (any status) is JSON: `{ importId?, status: "completed" | "rejected", total, created, errors: [ { row, column, code, message } ] }`
A row whose email equals an earlier row's in the same file gets `duplicate_in_file` ... A row whose email belongs to an existing user gets `already_exists`. Existing users are never modified.
role `member` (the product's non-admin default; OG-3)
the endpoint and the page run only for an authenticated user who is an admin at the time of the request (A-1).
verdicts.missing: Whether bulk import is a separate permission from single-user creation, i.e. that the ability is not implied by being able to create one user.

verdicts.quote: header lacks `email` or `name` (`missing_column`, `column` names it); an unknown column such as `role` (`unknown_column`); a repeated column (`duplicate_column`); header only (`no_rows`)
UTF-8 (a leading BOM is ignored), comma-separated, RFC 4180 quoting (double quote doubles to escape, quoted fields may contain commas), CRLF or LF line ends.
Nothing is emailed by this feature.
A file over the size limit gives 413 `file_too_large` ... more than the row maximum gives 422 `too_many_rows`. In both, the whole file is rejected
verdicts.missing: The numeric maximum file size and row count (OG-6 leaves S and L undecided).

verdicts.quote: 0-byte file (`empty_file`) ... header only (`no_rows`); R-5.B: a file with one row (`solo@example.com,Solo Sam`) gives `total: 1`, `created: 1`
Repeating a successful upload yields 422 with `already_exists` on every row and creates nothing new.
Processing is synchronous request/response (AD-1). | OG-6 shows volumes that cannot finish within one request.
verdicts.missing: Whether a maximum-size file can finish within one request; no background path or completion notification is defined if it cannot.

verdicts.quote: Nothing is emailed by this feature.
Imported users are created in a `pending` state with no password and cannot sign in until activated by a mechanism outside this spec (OG-4).
verdicts.missing: How a pending user first gets credentials and signs in (OG-4 open).

verdicts.quote: Uploaded file bytes: held in request memory only; never written to disk or the datastore, deleted when the request ends
Import audit record (one per request that passed R-1): `importId`, admin id, UTC timestamp, sanitised original file name ... `total`, `created`, outcome
Recovery: nothing to repair after failure; the admin fixes the file and re-uploads.
verdicts.missing: Whether a running import can be cancelled; retry is only a whole-file re-upload.

verdicts.quote: The bound on response time at L rows **is unresolved** (missing decision: L and an acceptable duration).
verdicts.missing: The time bound itself; progress is only a generic 'Uploading' indicator (R-8 state 3).

verdicts.quote: Existing users are never modified.
verdicts.missing: That single-user creation by hand keeps working unchanged.

verdicts.quote: no cell is evaluated or executed, and stored values are kept verbatim ... Spreadsheet-formula neutralisation matters on any future export and is out of scope here.
